extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX/TikZ users creating calendars, diagrams, and graphics (TikZ library users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and option reference for creating TikZ calendars, ER diagrams, folding diagrams, matrices, and mindmaps — describing styles, execution order, and options to control layout and rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: if (condition) {code} else {code}/options
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditionals in calendar specifications: if ((condition)){code} else {else code} and the \\ifdate{condition}{then code}{else code} form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code or options may be either code (surrounded by curly braces) or a list of TikZ options (surrounded by square brackets). If code, it is executed for the current day; if options, they are passed to a scope surrounding the current date. Examples: if (Sunday) {\draw...} else {\fill...} vs if (Sunday) [red] else [green]. Use \ifdate in normal code (described elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: date condition tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Date tests available for calendar conditionals: day names (Monday..Sunday), workday/weekend, equals (testing whether current date equals a given date), at least, at most, between, day of month, and similar comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions let you select dates or ranges (e.g., if (equals=2000-01-20) { ... } ). Use them with if/\ifdate to style or execute code on particular dates (examples show weekend, Sunday, at most/at least/between).

rubrics_metrics.name: current date code execution order
rubrics_metrics.description: For each date the current date code is executed; it consists of parts in this order: (1) before-scope code, (2) open a scope, (3) at-begin-scope code, (4) all date-ifs from the calendar specification, (5) at-end-scope code, (6) close the scope, (7) after-scope code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ordering matters because the current date code as a whole is not surrounded by a scope/TeX group, so code in before-scope and after-scope can 'leak' or have effects on following days. Use the different codes to control accumulation and scoping of transformations and styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: execute before day scope=(code)
rubrics_metrics.description: This code is executed before everything else for each date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple calls of this option are accumulative: the first call's code is used first for each day, then the second, etc. Use it to set up per-day state before the day scope runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: execute at begin day scope=(code)
rubrics_metrics.description: This code is executed at the beginning of the day scope (before everything else inside the scope).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects are accumulative if specified multiple times. Use it to position or style the day locally inside its scope (e.g., horizontal shifts by weekday).

rubrics_metrics.name: execute at end day scope=(code)
rubrics_metrics.description: This code is executed just before the day scope is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accumulation is in reverse order; useful to pair \scope and \endscope commands supplied via at-begin and at-end code. Use for operations that should happen inside the day's scope but at the end (e.g., finishing drawings).

rubrics_metrics.name: execute after day scope=(code)
rubrics_metrics.description: This code is executed at the very end of the current date, outside the day scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accumulation is in reverse order. Use for operations whose effects should persist/accumulate across days (e.g., shifting the origin to create lists of days).

rubrics_metrics.name: use of scope codes to create arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: By adjusting before/at-begin/at-end/after day scope code you can create different day arrangements (lists, week lists, month lists, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: to create a simple vertical list of days shift the coordinate system downward in execute after day scope so shifts accumulate across days. Be careful which codes are inside/outside the day scope to control accumulation and leakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=day list downward / day list upward
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined arrangement styles where days of a month are typeset one per line: day list downward makes the list grow downward; day list upward grows upward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The shift between days is given by day yshift; between months an additional shift of month yshift is added. Use month yshift to control vertical spacing between months.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=day list right / left
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined list arrangements that grow horizontally. day list right grows to the right (uses day xshift and month xshift); day list left grows to the left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use day xshift/month xshift for horizontal control.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=week list
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates one row for each week in the date range; days inside each week are placed according to weekday columns (Monday at first position by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses day xshift for distance between days in a week row and day yshift for distance between rows. If the range doesn't start on Monday, the first line starts in the appropriate column. At the start of each month (except the first) an extra vertical space month yshift is added; set month yshift=0pt for a continuous list.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=month list
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a row for each month where all days of a month are listed alongside each other, and columns are aligned by weekday (first column contains Mondays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Months that don't start on Monday are shifted to the right to align days into weekday columns; use month yshift for vertical spacing between month rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: month label placement options (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Month labels are not placed by default; use month text, every month, month code to change appearance and one of the month label style options to specify position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is no placement; choose left/right/above/below variants depending on arrangement and desired anchoring. Use the yshift option with the month node to fine-tune vertical placement; some placements have fixed offsets (e.g., above-left raises by 1.25em by default).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=month label left / left vertical
rubrics_metrics.description: month label left places the month label to the left of the first day of the month. month label left vertical rotates the label counterclockwise by 90 degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For week list and month list, if a month does not start on a Monday the position is chosen 'as if' the month had started on Monday (usually desired).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=month label right / right vertical
rubrics_metrics.description: month label right places the month label to the right of the row containing the first day (to the right of the first day in a day list, to the right of the first week in a week list, to the right of the whole month in a month list). right vertical rotates clockwise by 90 degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to place labels at the end of rows/rows-of-months.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=month label above left / above centered / above right
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions the month label above the row containing the first day; variants control horizontal alignment: left, centered, or right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: above-left is flushed left to the leftmost column and is raised by a fixed 1.25em by default; modify with month node yshift. Use above-centered to center the label above the row.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=month label below left / below centered
rubrics_metrics.description: Like above-left/centered but places the label below the row containing the first day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Below placements are more useful for some arrangements (e.g., day list right or month list) than for week list.

rubrics_metrics.name: use of \ifdate for conditional month/day code
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \ifdate{condition}{then code}{else code} in normal code to test date conditions (similar effect to the if (...) { } else { } calendar form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form is useful inside execute...scope code and outside the calendar specification; see page references for detailed description.

rubrics_metrics.name: style and option idiom for per-day adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: To position days (e.g., week list), combine execute at begin day scope to transform (e.g., \pgftransformxshift{\pgfcalendarcurrentweekday em}) and execute after day scope to move origin at week boundaries (e.g., move down on Sunday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show computing weekday offsets and shifting after weeks to create a grid where all Mondays align in one column.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=entity and style=every entity (ER diagrams)
rubrics_metrics.description: style=entity: use with nodes representing entity types; sets shape to rectangle, draws it, and sets sensible minimum size and width. style=every entity is invoked by entity and can be changed to alter all entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming is 'entity' though it represents entity types; you may redefine a style 'entity type' if naming bothers you. Change every entity to change appearance of all entity nodes (examples show color/fill/thickness tweaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=relationship and style=every relationship (ER diagrams)
rubrics_metrics.description: style=relationship: used for relationship (types) nodes; works like entity but for relationships. style=every relationship is used to customize relationships globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show using relationship nodes positioned and connected by edge commands to entity nodes; tweak every relationship for fill/draw/aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=attribute / style=key attribute / style=every attribute (ER diagrams)
rubrics_metrics.description: style=attribute marks a node as an attribute; connect attributes to entities via child or pin; style=key attribute intended for key attributes (by default typeset in italics). style=every attribute customizes attribute appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Underlining is a typical convention for key attributes but is hard to implement visually in TeX, so italics are used by default; change styles to alter fill/draw.

rubrics_metrics.name: \tikzfoldingdodecahedron command options
rubrics_metrics.description: \tikzfoldingdodecahedron[options]; options must be specified (nothing else between command name and semicolon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This command draws a folding diagram for a dodecahedron; options control geometry and per-face code. It is used to create paper folding diagrams (examples show calendars on faces).

rubrics_metrics.name: folding line length=(dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the length of the base line for folding; for the dodecahedron this is the length of all pentagon sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls scale of the folding diagram.

rubrics_metrics.name: face N=(code) for N=1..12
rubrics_metrics.description: face 1=... face 2=... ... face 12=... Each (code) is executed for the respective face with the coordinate system shifted/rotated so it lies at the middle of that face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to place content (nodes, calendars, etc.) on each face of the folding diagram (examples place a calendar on each face).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every cut and style=every fold
rubrics_metrics.description: style=every cut executed for every line that should be cut (empty by default). style=every fold executed for every line that should be folded (equal to help lines by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change these styles to color or change the line style for cuts and folds (examples show red cuts and dotted folds).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=matrix of nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds \node{ at the beginning and }; at the end of each cell, sets anchor to base, and gives nodes names matrixname-row-col (e.g., mymatrix-1-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saves verbosity when creating matrices of nodes. Use with examples to reference specific cells by name for drawing arrows or further styling.

rubrics_metrics.name: methods to add options to individual matrix cells (three methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1) Define row i column j style (e.g., row 2 column 3) to pass options to that cell. 2) Use cell syntax |[options]| (everything between bars passed to the node command); & also takes optional argument for extra column skip. 3) If a cell starts with a \path/\draw/\node/etc. command then the automatic \node{ ... }; wrappers are suppressed and full arbitrary content may be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three methods let you customize individual cells' appearance, names, and spacing; use |[options](name)| to both style and rename a node.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=matrix of math nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as matrix of nodes but adds $ at the beginning and end of each node so math mode is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for mathematical matrices where each cell is math content; combines with the cell customization methods above.

rubrics_metrics.name: nodes in empty cells=(true|false)
rubrics_metrics.description: When set to true a (empty) node is put in empty cells; normally empty cells are truly empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful together with matrix of nodes/math nodes and nodes={...} to enforce styling (e.g., draw circles) even for cells with no content.

rubrics_metrics.name: left delimiter=(delimiter) and right delimiter=(delimiter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add delimiters (any delimiter acceptable to TeX's \left) to the left and/or right of a node that has standard anchors north/south/etc.; implemented by measuring node height and adding correctly sized delimiters via after-node processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be applied to matrices or any rectangle-like node; examples show parentheses and custom delimiters, and setting styles for these delimiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every delimiter / every left delimiter / every right delimiter
rubrics_metrics.description: Styles executed for every delimiter (and specifically for left or right delimiters) allowing shifting, coloring, or other modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to globally adjust delimiter appearance/position (examples show xshift tweaks and coloring).

rubrics_metrics.name: above delimiter / below delimiter and style=every above/below delimiter
rubrics_metrics.description: Options to add a delimiter above or below a node (implemented by rotating a left delimiter); corresponding every- styles executed for each such delimiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow unusual delimiter placements (above/below) for decorative or specialized layouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=mindmap and style=every mindmap
rubrics_metrics.description: style=mindmap installs many internal settings useful for drawing mindmaps; style=every mindmap is included and can be changed to add special settings to mindmaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mindmap style on a picture/scope; the library defines sizes of concepts so a medium-size mindmap fits an A4 page. Examples show concept nodes and child/grow placement; tweak style=every mindmap to change global appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: predefined concept sizes and large mindmap
rubrics_metrics.description: Sizes of concepts are predefined so a medium-size mindmap will fit on an A4 page; there is also a 'large mindmap' variant to make larger layouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate mindmap size/style to match page/print constraints; examples show concept color and child growth directions.
